title: Social responsibility in staffing

match.reason: The closest bank point, Corporate social responsibility, covers CSR across society and the environment in general, while this point is narrower, about fairly treating staff, including overseas recruits, beyond legal requirements, so no bank point teaches this same idea.

draft.title: Social responsibility in staffing
card: Social responsibility means a business acts ethically towards people, not only as the law requires. In staffing, it means treating workers fairly and with respect.
The law sets a minimum, such as the minimum pay and conditions for employees. A socially responsible business may choose to go further than this minimum.
Examples include paying a fair wage, giving clear and honest information about the job, and offering safe and supportive workplaces.

The same applies to staff recruited from overseas. They may be new to Australia and unsure of their rights, so a responsible business explains the job clearly, pays them properly and does not take advantage of them.
draft.remember: Social responsibility in staffing is treating workers fairly, even where the law does not demand it.

a.q: Which action shows social responsibility in staffing, rather than only meeting a legal minimum?
opts: Helping new staff understand their pay and rights
Paying exactly the legal minimum and nothing more
Hiring only the number of staff the law requires
Keeping records only when an inspector asks for them
a.why: A responsible business goes beyond the minimum by helping staff understand their pay and rights. Paying exactly the legal minimum is lawful, but it does not go beyond what the law requires.
a.clue: Look for the choice that goes further than the legal minimum.

b.q: Priya runs a bakery in Geelong and hires a baker from overseas. Which choice is the most socially responsible?
opts: Explain the job and pay in plain terms before they start
Pay the legal minimum and say little about the job
Offer a lower wage because they are new to Australia
Tell them rights are covered only by what they sign
b.why: Explaining the job and pay clearly treats the new worker fairly and helps them know their rights. Paying the legal minimum can be lawful, but saying little does not show care, and the other options take advantage of the worker.
b.clue: A new arrival may not know their rights, so what would a fair employer do?

a.best: Helping new staff understand their pay and rights

b.best: Explain the job and pay in plain terms before they start

problems.detail: The card lists 'offering safe and supportive workplaces' as going further than the legal minimum. A safe workplace is a legal duty under Victoria's Occupational Health and Safety Act 2004, which is point 3. Students could think safety is optional. Make it 'supportive' only, or say that safety beyond the legal duties is the extra step.

Employers must already give new employees the Fair Work Information Statement and payslips, so giving information about pay and rights is partly a legal requirement. The correct option and the why present it as wholly beyond the law. Wording such as 'Taking time to explain their pay and rights in plain terms' would make the extra step clearer.

check.summary: Answers are clear and correct. The card wrongly presents safe workplaces as beyond the law, though workplace safety is a legal duty (point 3). Question a's right option partly overlaps the legal duty to give new staff the Fair Work Information Statement.

proposal.title: Social responsibility in staffing
card: Social responsibility means a business acts ethically towards people, not only as the law requires. In staffing, it means treating workers fairly and with respect.
The law sets a minimum for every employer, such as minimum pay, payslips and a safe workplace. A socially responsible business may choose to go further than this minimum.
Going further could mean paying above the minimum wage, taking time to explain pay and rights in plain terms, or offering a supportive workplace with training and flexible hours.

The same applies to staff recruited from overseas. They may be new to Australia and unsure of their rights, so a responsible business explains the job clearly, pays them properly and does not take advantage of them.
proposal.remember: Social responsibility in staffing is treating workers fairly, even where the law does not demand it.

a.q: Which action shows social responsibility in staffing, rather than only meeting a legal minimum?
opts: Taking time to explain pay and rights in plain terms
Handing over only the documents the law requires
Paying exactly the legal minimum and nothing more
Meeting the safety duties the law sets for employers
a.why: Explaining pay and rights in plain terms goes beyond simply handing over the documents the law requires. The other three are lawful, but each one only meets the legal minimum rather than going further.
a.clue: Which choice adds something the law does not ask for?
